WTH?? Investigation Launched After Wooden Box Was Found In A New York Elementary School, Allegedly Used To Lock Special Needs Students Inside
Audio By Carbonatix
An investigation was launched after a wooden box was found in the corner of a New York elementary school classroom, allegedly used to lock special needs kids inside.
The investigation was launched after photos of the box began circulating on Facebook.
"I’m so sick of the sh*t that is allowed to happen at the St. Regis Mohawk school UNDER the so-called leadership of Allison Benedict," local Chrissy Jacobs said on Facebook.
"This 'box' was built for special needs students. This is sick! ... These children do not deserve to be traumatized while y'all are being paid to educate and protect them!"
Gov. Kathy Hochul has since responded to the allegations, saying they raise "serious questions regarding the safety of children," calling for the Education Department to investigate.
"These allegations are alarming and entirely unacceptable," she said.
